text.p: Argentina's political alliance between the center-left Frepaso party and centrist Radicals has the overwhelming support of the population, according to a MORI poll published in La Nacion Wednesday.

The poll, carried out before the Frepaso-Radical alliance was announced this weekend, found that 77 percent of respondents considered a possible union positive after this October's mid-term elections, said La Nacion.
Nine percent of respondents where ambivalent about the alliance, four percent were negative and 10 percent did not know.
The pollsters asked voters the same question about the 1999 presidential elections and once again there was a large majority of 69 percent in favor of the opposition working together.

Political analysts said the ground breaking alliance of the Peronist government's main opposition parties means the Peronists are no longer guaranteed their majority in the lower house of Congress after October elections.
The poll, of 1,000 people, was carried out in the province of Buenos Aires from June 14 to June 28. There was a three percent margin of error.
Another MORI poll in the new business daily, Buenos Aires Economico, found that voters also back Argentina's Convertibility plan pegging the value of the peso to the dollar at par.

Asked for how long the country should continue with Convertibility, 55 percent of respondents said it should be kept forever, 13 percent said the country should leave the peg but they do not know when. Only seven percent said the system has to be ended as soon as possible.
The poll was carried out in the Buenos Aires province during the last week of July. There were 1,000 people polled and there was a three percent margin of error.
